content: In the language of India: Śatasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā. In the language of Tibet: A flawless condensation of the meaning of the Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Verses.Homage to the Mother who gives birth to all.Thus have I heard at one time. The Blessed One, having arisen from the meditative absorption called "Profound Illumination," was dwelling at Vulture Peak Mountain near Rājagṛha together with a great community of about five thousand monks. All of them were arhats—those who had exhausted their defilements, were without afflictions, had attained mastery, whose minds were thoroughly liberated, who were of noble breed, great elephants, who had done what was to be done, had accomplished their task, had laid down the burden, had attained their own goal, and had completely exhausted the fetters of existence. They were with the bodhisattva mahāsattvas whose minds were thoroughly liberated by perfect knowledge, as well as the noble Avalokiteśvara, Rab-'byor, and Kun-dga'-bo, and countless other beings including gods and humans. The Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha Śākyamuni, then beheld and emitted sixty million rays of light.Then, he became fully adorned with the thirty-two excellent marks and the eighty secondary signs. The venerable ones offered prostrations and demonstrated various ways of making offerings. Then, the Blessed One said to the venerable ones: "Just as the noble Avalokiteśvara, Subhūti, and the bodhisattva mahāsattvas will surely emerge into the perfection of wisdom, you should train in the same way. The six objects and the five aggregates: form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness; the twelve sense sources and the six faculties: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; and forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and phenomena. The meaning of consciousness is: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. The meaning of contact is: eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact. The meaning of feeling conditioned by contact is: feeling conditioned by eye-contact, feeling conditioned by ear-contact, feeling conditioned by nose-contact, feeling conditioned by tongue-contact, feeling conditioned by body-contact, and feeling conditioned by mind-contact. The meaning of the six elements is: earth element, water element, fire element, wind element, space element, and consciousness element. The meaning of the twelve links of dependent origination is: ignorance, formations, consciousness, name and form, the six sense sources, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, and aging and death. The meaning of the twelve sense sources of the agent is: self, sentient being, life, wanderer, sustainer, person, individual, possessor of strength, possessor of the self, agent, feeler, knower, and seer."There are the gods of the desire realm. There are the gods of the Four Great Kings class. There are the gods of the Thirty-three. There are the gods of the Yāma. There are the gods of Tuṣita. There are the gods of Nirmaṇarati. There are the gods of Paranirmitavaśavartin. There are the gods of the seventeen classes of the form realm. There are the gods of Brahmakāyika. There are the gods of Brahmapurohita. There are the gods of Mahābrahmā. There are the gods of Parīttābha. There are the gods of Apramāṇābha. There are the gods of Ābhāsvara. There are the gods of Parīttaśubha. There are the gods of Apramāṇaśubha. There are the gods of Śubhakṛtsna. There are the gods of Anabhraka. There are the gods of Puṇyaprasava. There are the gods of Bṛhatphala. There are the gods of Asañjnisattva. There are the gods of Avṛha. There are the gods of Atapa. There are the gods of Sudṛśa. There are the gods of Sudarśana. There are the gods of Akaniṣṭha. There are the gods of the four formless spheres. There are the gods of the sphere of infinite space. There are the gods of the sphere of infinite consciousness. There are the gods of the sphere of nothingness. There are the gods of the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception.The perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, the perfection of wisdom, inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner and outer emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, the emptiness of the ultimate, the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, the emptiness of that which transcends limits, the emptiness of that without beginning or end, the emptiness of non-repudiation, the emptiness of nature, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-entities, the emptiness of essential nature, and the emptiness of the essential nature of non-entities; the four foundations of mindfulness, the four correct exertions, the four legs of miraculous action, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven branches of enlightenment, the noble eightfold path, the four noble truths, the four meditative concentrations, the four immeasurables, the four formless absorptions, the eight liberations, the nine successive absorptions, the gateways to liberation of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, the five clairvoyances, the concentrations, the gateways of dhāraṇī, the ten powers of the Tathāgata, and the teaching on the meaning of the liberations—these, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, are the purity of form, the purity of feeling, the purity of perception, the purity of formative factors, the purity of consciousness, the purity of the eye, the purity of the ear, the purity of the nose, the purity of the tongue, the purity of the body, and the purity of the mind; furthermore, Rab-'byor, through the complete purity of form, sound is completely pure; through the complete purity of sound, odor is completely pure; through the complete purity of odor, taste is completely pure; through the complete purity of taste, touch is completely pure; through the complete purity of touch, phenomena are completely pure; and through the complete purity of phenomena, the eye-consciousness is completely pure, up to the complete purity of the mind-consciousness.The four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy, great equanimity, the eighteen unshared dharmas of a buddha, the fruit of a stream-enterer, the fruit of a once-returner, the fruit of a non-returner, the state of an arhat, pratyekabuddhahood, the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and all-aspect omniscience—these lead to the realization of the wisdom that is unobstructed and unattached regarding the past.When the Blessed One had spoken thus, the assembly of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, Rab-'byor, Kun-dga'-bo, the venerable ones, their community of monks, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, gandharvas, kumbhāṇḍas, and mahoragas rejoiced and highly praised what the Blessed One had said.The summary of the meaning of the Great Mother, the Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines, arranged in verses, is complete.
